record.paper_title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes: consequences and open questions
record.context_brief: Hyperuniform SSEP activity SCGF beyond diffusive scaling
record.original_question: For the periodic Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process with L sites, fixed particle density ρ, activity K equal to the total number of jumps, and activity counting field s, determine the scaled cumulant generating function ψ_K^SSEP(s) in the hyperuniform large-activity regime s > 0 with s of order one, beyond the diffusive Edwards-Wilkinson scaling s = λ/L². Equivalently, can the ASEP-current cumulant series obtained from the mapping ψ_K^SSEP(s) = (2/(p+q)) ψ_Q^ASEP(µ), with e^{-2µ} = p/q and e^{-s} = cosh(µ), be resummed or transformed despite divergences when q/p approaches roots of unity, and can one obtain a positive-s parametric representation analogous to the known negative-s representation?

evidence.quote:
Understanding how the SCGF behaves for s > 0 (beyond the
diﬀusive regime) is not trivial and still an open question, as we detail in the next subsection.

We were not able to perform a resummation or
a transformation of this series that would allow one to cure this behavior.

The question of computing the series (3.33) for s > 0 thus remains open, and would yield an interesting
description of the hyperuniform phase beyond the diﬀusive regime described in Sec. 3.2. The aim would
be to ﬁnd the equivalent of the parametric representation of Eqs. (3.18)-(3.21) for ψSSEP
K (s), but valid for
s > 0.

The
question remains open to understand how the series (3.33) can be resummed in order to understand how
the SCGF ψSSEP
K (s) behaves in the hyperuniform regime s > 0 for s = O(L0) (i.e. beyond the diﬀusive
regime). Since the singularities occur when q
p are unit roots, it would be interesting to see if the results
of Refs. [117–120] could be used in some way.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process (SSEP) on a periodic ring of L sites at fixed particle density ρ ∈ (0,1): each site holds at most one particle, and every particle independently attempts jumps to each neighboring site at rate 1, the jump being performed only if the target site is empty. Let K(t) denote the dynamical activity, i.e. the total number of jumps performed by the system up to time t, and define the scaled cumulant generating function (SCGF) of the activity by

  ψ_K^SSEP(s) = lim_{t→∞} (1/t) log E[ e^{-s K(t)} ].

The "diffusive" (Edwards–Wilkinson) regime corresponds to scaling s = λ/L² with λ fixed; in this regime ψ_K^SSEP(s) is well understood, including a hyperuniform phase for sufficiently negative λ. The problem concerns the complementary regime where s is of order one with s > 0 (beyond the diffusive scaling).

A formal mapping relates ψ_K^SSEP(s) to the SCGF ψ_Q^ASEP(µ) of the integrated current Q in the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) with forward/backward hop rates p, q on the same ring at the same density, via

  ψ_K^SSEP(s) = (2/(p+q)) · ψ_Q^ASEP(µ),    with    e^{-2µ} = p/q,    e^{-s} = cosh(µ).

Expanding ψ_Q^ASEP(µ) as a cumulant series in µ produces, on the SSEP side, a series in s whose coefficients diverge whenever q/p approaches a root of unity, preventing a direct termwise interpretation for s > 0.

Determine ψ_K^SSEP(s) for s > 0 with s = O(1) as L → ∞. Equivalently, find a resummation or analytic transformation of the ASEP cumulant series that resolves the root-of-unity singularities, and produce a parametric representation of ψ_K^SSEP(s) valid for s > 0 analogous to the parametric representation known for s < 0, thereby describing the hyperuniform phase beyond the diffusive regime.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on large deviations of activity/current in SSEP and ASEP (e.g. SciPost Phys. 17.2.033 and follow-up studies on topological phases in SSEP dynamics) continues to discuss the hyperuniform phase and the diffusive Edwards–Wilkinson regime, but no resummation of the ASEP cumulant series yielding ψ_K^SSEP(s) for s = O(1) > 0, nor a parametric representation valid for positive s, appears to have been obtained. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes
status_evidence.snippet: Hyperuniform phase is surprisingly difficult to study beyond the diffusive regime; SCGF behavior for s>0 beyond diffusive regime not trivial and still an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The behavior of the activity SCGF beyond the diffusive regime is described as still open.

status_evidence.title: Large deviations in the symmetric simple exclusion process (SciPost Phys. 17.2.033)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies SSEP large deviations including activity and hyperuniformity within diffusive scaling.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent SSEP large-deviation literature does not provide ψ_K^SSEP(s) for s=O(1)>0.

status_evidence.title: Topological phases in the dynamics of the simple exclusion process
status_evidence.snippet: Studies dynamical phases of SSEP related to activity biasing.
status_evidence.claim: Newer studies address related dynamical-phase questions but do not resolve the positive-s SCGF problem.
